children.value: , we can start by finding the determinant - expanding down the first column, to take advantage of the zero entry:

children.html: det⁡(1−2302−431−4)=1∣2−41−4∣+3∣−232−4∣=−4+3⋅2=2\begin{align*} \det \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 1 & -4 \end{pmatrix} &= 1 \begin{vmatrix} 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -4 \end{vmatrix} + 3 \begin{vmatrix} -2 & 3 \\ 2 & -4 \end{vmatrix} = -4 + 3 \cdot 2 = 2 \end{align*}det⎝⎛​103​−221​3−4−4​⎠⎞​​=1∣∣​21​−4−4​∣∣​+3∣∣​−22​3−4​∣∣​=−4+3⋅2=2​

children.value: Then we find the adjoint matrix, by calculating the matrix of cofactors and transposing it:

children.html: adj⁡(1−2302−431−4)=(−4−12−6−5−13−7242)T=(−4−52−12−134−6−72),∴A−1=12(−4−52−12−134−6−72).\begin{align*} \operatorname{adj} \begin{pmatrix} 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 \\ 3 & 1 & -4 \end{pmatrix} &= \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -12 & -6 \\ -5 & -13 & -7 \\ 2 & 4 & 2 \end{pmatrix}^\mathsf{T} = \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -5 & 2 \\ -12 & -13 & 4 \\ -6 & -7 & 2 \end{pmatrix}, \\ \therefore A^{-1} &= \frac{1}{2} \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -5 & 2 \\ -12 & -13 & 4 \\ -6 & -7 & 2 \end{pmatrix}. \end{align*}adj⎝⎛​103​−221​3−4−4​⎠⎞​∴A−1​=⎝⎛​−4−52​−12−134​−6−72​⎠⎞​T=⎝⎛​−4−12−6​−5−13−7​242​⎠⎞​,=21​⎝⎛​−4−12−6​−5−13−7​242​⎠⎞​.​

x=12(−4−52−12−134−6−72)(−787)=12(280)=(140).\begin{align*} \mathbf{x} &= \frac{1}{2} \begin{pmatrix} -4 & -5 & 2 \\ -12 & -13 & 4 \\ -6 & -7 & 2 \end{pmatrix} \begin{pmatrix}-7 \\ 8 \\ 7 \end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{2} \begin{pmatrix} 2 \\ 8 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix} 1 \\4 \\ 0 \end{pmatrix}. \end{align*}x​=21​⎝⎛​−4−12−6​−5−13−7​242​⎠⎞​⎝⎛​−787​⎠⎞​=21​⎝⎛​280​⎠⎞​=⎝⎛​140​⎠⎞​.​
